name: Passport (Fresh Application)
department: Ministry of External Affairs — Passport Seva
summary: Apply for a fresh Indian passport for international travel through the Passport Seva Kendra network.
eligibility: Indian citizens of any age (minors apply through a parent/guardian)
No pending criminal proceedings or court orders barring travel/passport issuance
documents: Proof of address (Aadhaar, utility bill, rent agreement, etc.)
Proof of date of birth (birth certificate, PAN, matriculation certificate, or Aadhaar)
Annexures/affidavits for special cases (e.g. minors, name change, ECR category)
fee: ₹2,500 for a fresh 36-page passport (normal processing); ₹5,000 under Tatkaal. A 60-page passport and other categories cost more. A 10% concession applies to fresh applications for children up to 8 years and senior citizens over 60. Fees increased from ₹1,500/₹3,500 effective 1 July 2026 under the Passports (Amendment) Rules, 2026.
process: Register on the Passport Seva portal and fill the online application form
Pay the fee online and book an appointment at a Passport Seva Kendra (PSK) or Post Office PSK
Visit the centre with original documents for verification and biometric capture
Police verification is conducted (pre- or post-issuance depending on category)
Track status online; passport is dispatched by post once cleared
source: Ministry of External Affairs, Passports (Amendment) Rules, 2026

faq.question: How long does a normal passport application take?
faq.answer: Typically 2-3 weeks after police verification is cleared, though this varies by city and category. Tatkaal applications are faster, often within a week.

faq.question: Did passport fees increase in 2026?
faq.answer: Yes. Under the Passports (Amendment) Rules, 2026 (notified 20 June 2026, effective 1 July 2026), the fresh 36-page normal passport fee rose from ₹1,500 to ₹2,500, and Tatkaal from ₹3,500 to ₹5,000.

changeLog.summary: Fresh 36-page normal passport fee increased from ₹1,500 to ₹2,500; Tatkaal from ₹3,500 to ₹5,000, under the Passports (Amendment) Rules, 2026.
